subject: dsa
title: Find the Duplicate Number
summary: Read the array as a linked list where index i points to index nums[i]. A repeated value makes two arrows merge into a cycle, so Floyd's slow/fast pointers find it. The cycle's entrance index is the duplicate value.
problem: An array of n+1 values in 1..n has exactly one duplicate; find it without modifying the array or using extra space.

steps.caption: Values lie in 1..n with one duplicate. Read the array as a linked list (i -> nums[i]); the duplicate is where two arrows merge into a cycle.
Floyd's two pointers both start at index 0. Each round, slow takes one step (i -> nums[i]) and fast takes two.
Round 1: slow lands on index 1 (nums[0]=1); fast takes two hops to index 3 (0 -> 1 -> 3).
Round 2: slow steps to index 3 (nums[1]=3); fast takes two hops to index 4 (3 -> 2 -> 4).
Round 3: slow steps to index 2 (nums[3]=2); fast circles the cycle and stays at index 4 (4 -> 2 -> 4).
Round 4: both land on index 4. Slow and fast meeting inside the cycle proves a cycle exists.
Phase 2: send slow back to index 0 and leave fast at the meeting point. Now advance both one step at a time.
Stepping both one at a time, they meet at index 2, the entrance where the cycle's tail joins the loop.
The entrance is index 2, and that index number is the repeated value. So the duplicate is 2.
